x-bump-note: 3.0.0 -> 3.0.1 (patch): ZERO SHAPE EFFECT on record validation. The `x-external-consumers` annotation now names a reader class instead of a repo; the roster of consuming repos lives in the RESEARCH-CLAIMS-JSON-IS-AN-EXTERNAL-CONTRACT tripwire page. DR-097 push-side duty ATTACHES (the engine repo vendors this schema): the hold is HOLDING until the engine repo re-vendors 3.0.1; RE-VENDOR pending, the mirror is at 3.0.0 meanwhile. PRIOR: 2.0.0 -> 3.0.0 (require-id) promotes `id` to `required` alongside `claim_text`. Same ground: the artifact declares itself a durable queryable index, and a record with no key is unaddressable in one. Zero producer cost — `id` is populated on 259/259 records across every claims file on this machine, and every producer template assigns it. A separate version from 2.0.0 rather than a revision of it because 2.0.0 was already pushed and its consumer memo already sent; a redefined version number is worse for a pinning consumer than a second bump. `source_url` is NOT promoted despite the same argument applying: the three producer paths disagree on it in prose (specialist-prompt-template.md:242 mandates it with a `training_knowledge` sentinel; repo-synthesizer-prompt-template.md:314 mandates a file:line value; notebooklm/worker-prompt-template.md:82 explicitly permits null), and the sentinel form contradicts this schema's own tripwire rule against placeholder citations. Requiring it means settling that three-way disagreement first — tracked separately, not smuggled into a schema bump. PRIOR: 1.1.0 -> 2.0.0 (require-claim-text, cross-repo/inbox/2026-08-30-the game-editor server-em-research-claims-hook-rejects-array.md) moves `claim_text` from declared-only into `required`. MAJOR because it constrains producers: a record omitting it now fails claims_emit.emit_claims per-record validation (exit 1) rather than landing clean. Readers are unaffected — a required constraint only narrows what reaches them, so no consumer pinning 1.1.0 loses a field. WHY: a producer emitted `claim` rather than `claim_text` and, with `required: []`, shipped a 59-record file that was schema-valid and semantically empty — every record would have queried as a claim with no text, silently, to a declared external consumer. Second instance of the class (source_url/source_date sat declared-but-unpopulated before it), and the RESEARCH-CLAIMS-JSON-IS-AN-EXTERNAL-CONTRACT tripwire's rule against it had no mechanism discharging it. `claim_text` is the one field whose absence makes a record meaningless, so it is the one required; producer-local extra keys stay permitted (`additionalProperties` deliberately unset) because producers legitimately carry their own fields alongside the contract's. `id` is required on the same ground: the artifact declares itself a durable queryable index, and a record with no key is unaddressable in one. Zero producer cost — it is populated on 259/259 records across every claims file on this machine, and every producer template assigns it. `source_url` is NOT promoted despite the same argument applying: the three producer paths disagree on it in prose (specialist-prompt-template.md:242 mandates it with a `training_knowledge` sentinel; repo-synthesizer-prompt-template.md:314 mandates a file:line value; notebooklm/worker-prompt-template.md:82 explicitly permits null), and the sentinel form contradicts this schema's own tripwire rule against placeholder citations. Requiring it means settling that three-way disagreement first — tracked separately, not smuggled into a schema bump.
description: Per-claim queryable record promoted from claims.json (N records per file; synthetic enumeration in query-records C5). PUBLISHED READ CONTRACT: docs/research/*.claims.json is consumed read-only by external sibling repos pinning x-schema-version; field removals and semantic changes require a major bump plus a cross-repo memo to declared consumers.

id.description: Unique identifier for this claim within its claims.json file.

claim_text.description: The full text of the claim as emitted by the specialist producer.

confidence.description: Producer-assessed confidence level for this claim.

source_url.description: URL of the primary source supporting this claim.

source_date.description: Publication or retrieval date of the source (YYYY-MM-DD).

topic_tags.description: List of topic tags assigned by the producer to categorise this claim.

type.description: Semantic type of the claim as classified by the producer.

evidence.description: Supporting evidence quoted or summarised by the producer (optional).

counter_evidence.description: Counter-evidence or caveats noted by the producer (optional).

corroborated_by.description: Reference to another source or claim that corroborates this one (optional).

contested_by.description: Reference to a source or claim that contests this one (optional).
